Rashi on Zevachim 4a:10:1.hebrew: וישנן בחטאות הפנימיות - אבל זריקת מזבח החיצון לית בהו:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:10:1.english: And they are [performed] in the inner sin offerings - But the sprinkling [of blood] on the outer altar is not found in them.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:13:1.hebrew: זריקה זר חייב עליה מיתה - אבל שחיטה כשרה בזר, וקבלה והולכה אע"פ שפסולה בזר, אין חייב עליה מיתה. כדאמרי' בסדר יומא (דף כד.): ארבעה עבודות זר חייב עליהם מיתה: זריקה, והקטרה, וניסוך המים, והיין. דכתיב גבי "והזר הקרב יומת", "ועבדתם עבודת מתנה", ודרשינן: עבודת מתנה, ולא עבודת סילוק; "ועבדתם עבודה תמה", ולא עבודה שיש אחריה עבודה. והני כולהו יש אחריהם עבודה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:13:1.english: Sprinkling — a non-priest is liable to death for it - But slaughter is valid when performed by a non-priest; and receiving and conveying [the blood], although invalid when performed by a non-priest, [a non-priest] is not liable to death for them. As we say in the order of Yoma (24a): A non-priest is liable to death for four services: sprinkling, burning [on the altar], the libation of water, and [the libation of] wine. For it is written regarding [these]: "and the non-priest who approaches shall be put to death"; "and you shall perform the service of a gift," and we derive: a service of gift, but not a service of removal; "and you shall perform the service," [meaning] a complete service, but not a service that has another service after it. And all of these have another service after them.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:15:1.hebrew: מכולהו - במה הצד השוה שבהן, שהן עבודה וצריכה לשמה, אף אני אביא הולכה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:15:1.english: From all of them - What is the common feature among them? That they are a rite and require being performed for its own sake; so too I will include conveying the blood.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:15:2.hebrew: הולכה אפשר לבטלה - שאם רצה, שוחט בצד המזבח וזורק, כדתניא במתניתין (לקמן זבחים דף יג.):
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:15:2.english: Conveying [the blood] can be dispensed with - For if one wished, he may slaughter beside the altar and throw [the blood], as we learned in the Mishnah (below, Zevachim 13a).

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:16:1.hebrew: והקריבו זו קבלת הדם - "ושחט את בן הבקר, והקריבו בני אהרן הכהנים", זו קבלה. דהא בתר שחיטה כתיב, ולא אפשר לאוקומיה בהולכה. ואף על גב דלשון הולכה הוא, כדחזינן בהולכת אברים דכתיב ביה הקרבה, ולשון הולכה היא:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:16:1.english: "And they shall present" – this is the collection of the blood - "And he shall slaughter the young bull, and Aaron's sons, the priests, shall present" — this is collection, for it is written after the slaughter, and it is impossible to establish it as referring to conveying. And even though it is an expression of conveying, as we see with the conveying of the limbs, regarding which "presenting" is written, and it is an expression of conveying:

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:16:2.hebrew: ה"ג ואפקיה רחמנא קבלה בלשון הולכה למימרא דהולכה לא תפקה מכלל קבלה: שינוי בעלים מנלן - שצריך לשוחטו על מנת שיתכפרו בו בעליו, לא שיתכפר בו אחר. דקתני לקמן (זבחים דף מו:): לשם ששה דברים הזבח נזבח, לשם זובח. מנלן דבעינן לשם זובח:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:16:2.english: So we read: "And the Merciful One expressed collection in the language of conveying, to say that you should not exclude conveying from the category of collection." [The Gemara asks:] From where do we derive [the law of] a change of owners? - That one must slaughter it with the intention that its owners be atoned through it, not that another be atoned through it. For it teaches later (Zevachim 46b): The offering is slaughtered for the sake of six things — for the sake of the one who offers it. From where do we derive that we require [that it be] for the sake of the one who offers it?

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:18:1.english: Zevah Todat Shelamav - meaning, its slaughter should be for the sake of a thanks offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:19:1.hebrew: זבח תודת שלמיו - שתהא זביחתו לשם תודה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:19:1.english: The sacrifice of his thanksgiving peace offering - That its slaughter be for the sake of a thanksgiving offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:19:2.english: Fit - And they are offered up as [the offering] of obligation:

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:19:3.hebrew: פסולה - כלומר, לא עלו לשם חובה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:19:3.english: Unfit - That is to say, they [the offerings] do not ascend [as valid] for the sake of the obligation.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:19:4.hebrew: תודה קרויה שלמים - כדכתיב "תודת שלמיו", כמו "חטאת הקהל" (ויקרא ד׳:כ״א), "תורת משה עבדי" (מלאכי ג׳:כ״ב):
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:19:4.english: A thanks offering is called a peace offering - As it is written, "his thanksgiving peace offering," like "the sin offering of the assembly" (Leviticus 4:21) [and] "the Torah of Moses My servant" (Malachi 3:22).

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:1:1.hebrew: ומנלן דבעינן זביחה לשמה - לכתחילה, דאי ממוצא שפתיך לא מיפרשי ביה עבודות:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:1:1.english: And from where do we [derive] that we require slaughter to be for its own sake - [That is,] ab initio (לכתחילה); for if [one were to derive it] from "that which issues from your lips," the [sacrificial] services are not specified in it.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:20:1.english: We are speaking of “the sacrifice of thanksgiving” - Our derivation is from this, while Abba Ḥanin’s is from “the thanksgiving of his peace offerings.”

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:21:1.hebrew: חטאת ואשם מנין - בת"כ קתני לה גבי האי קרא: ״ובשר זבח תודת שלמיו ביום קרבנו יאכל״, למדנו לתודה שנאכלת ליום ולילה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:21:1.english: From where [is it derived that] a sin offering and a guilt offering [are eaten for only a day and a night]? - In the Torat Kohanim (Sifra) it is taught alongside this verse: "And the meat of the sacrifice of his thanksgiving peace offering shall be eaten on the day of his offering." We have learned that the thanks offering is eaten for a day and a night.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:21:2.english: From where is a sin offering and a guilt offering derived? - The verse states 'zevaḥ'.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:25:1.hebrew: לא חלקת - דהא כולהו איתרבו לעיל:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:25:1.english: You did not differentiate - For all of them were included above.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:26:1.hebrew: שכן פסולו בגופו - לקמן מפרש לה ואזיל:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:26:1.english: For its disqualification is in its body - [Rashi] will explain this later as [the Gemara] proceeds.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:26:2.hebrew: וישנו בד' עבודות - שאם שחט שלא לשמו, או קיבל והלך וזרק שלא לשמו, אע"פ שלא חישב אלא על השחיטה שלא לשמו — פסול, כדרבינן להו לעיל. אבל שינוי בעלים לא שייך אלא בזריקה, דהא דרבינן שחיטה לפסול בשינוי בעלים אינו אלא כגון ששחט על מנת לזרוק להתכפר בו אחר. אבל שחט שלא לשם בעליו ולא הזכיר על מנת לזרוק, אין זו מחשבה, דשנוי בעלים לא שייך בקרבן אלא להתכפר בו, וכפרה בזריקה היא. והכי אמרי' לקמן בפרקין (זבחים דף י.) שאם אמר הריני שוחט לשם פלוני — כשר, שחטו על מנת לזרוק לשם פלוני — פסול. וכן לענין קבלה והולכה לא שייך שינוי בעלים, אא"כ חישב לקבל על מנת לזרוק לשם אחר:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:26:2.english: And it applies to four rites - For if one slaughtered not for its own sake, or received [the blood] and carried it and sprinkled it not for its own sake, even though he intended not for its own sake only with respect to the slaughter, it is disqualified, as we derived above. But deviation with regard to the owner is relevant only to the sprinkling; for the fact that we included slaughter to be disqualified by deviation with regard to the owner is only where, for example, he slaughtered with the intent to sprinkle so that another would be atoned by it. But if he slaughtered not for the sake of its owner and did not mention [that he intended] to sprinkle, this is not a [disqualifying] thought, since deviation with regard to the owner is relevant to an offering only for the purpose of atonement through it, and atonement is through the sprinkling. And so we say later in this chapter (Zevachim 10a) that if he said, "I am slaughtering for the sake of so-and-so," it is valid; [if] he slaughtered it with the intent to sprinkle for the sake of so-and-so, it is disqualified. Likewise, with regard to receiving and carrying, deviation with regard to the owner is not relevant unless he intended to receive [the blood] with the intent to sprinkle it for the sake of another.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:27:1.hebrew: וישנו לאחר מיתה - המפריש קרבנו ומת, והיורש מקריבו — שייך בו שינוי קדש, אבל לא שינוי בעלים, שהרי מתו בעליו:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:27:1.english: And it applies after death - One who set aside his offering and died, and his heir brings it — deviation [from the type of] offering applies to it, but not deviation [with regard to the] owner, since its owner has died.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:27:2.hebrew: וישנו בצבור - אבל שנוי בעלים לא שייך בקרבן צבור, שהרי הכל בעליו:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:27:2.english: And it applies to a communal [offering] - But a change of owner is not relevant to a communal offering, since everyone is its owner.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:2:1.english: From where [do we know] that “sacrifice” is called that with regard to slaughter? Perhaps [it] is simply their name - “A sacrifice of peace offerings” is said, and “sacrifice” was not stated because of slaughter.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:5:1.hebrew: מה לזביחה שכן פוסלת שלא לשם אוכלין בפסח - שאם שחטו שלא לאוכלין, כגון לחולה ולזקן שאין יכולין לאכול כזית, פסול, ואפילו הן בעליו, דכתיב "איש לפי אכלו" — אכילה בכזית. ושאר עבודות לא פסלי שלא לאוכלין, דכתיב "תכוסו". ותניא (פסחים דף סא.) רבי אומר: לשון סורסי הוא זה, כאדם האומר לחבירו "כוס לי טלה זה". והכי אמרינן בפסחים (דף עח:) דאין (מחשבה) אוכלין בזריקה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:5:1.english: What about slaughter, that it disqualifies [when done] not for the sake of those who eat, in the case of the Paschal offering - For if one slaughtered it not for those who eat it, such as for a sick person or an elderly person who cannot eat an olive-bulk, it is disqualified, even if they are its owners, as it is written: "each man according to his eating" (Exodus 12:4) — [meaning] eating of an olive-bulk. But the other rites are not disqualified [by intent] not for those who eat, as it is written: "you shall be counted [tikhosu]" (Exodus 12:4). And it is taught (Pesachim 61a): Rabbi says: This is an Aramaic [Syriac] expression, like a person who says to his fellow, "Slaughter [kus] this lamb for me." And so we say in Pesachim (78b) that there is no [disqualifying] intention regarding eaters in the case of the sprinkling.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:6:1.hebrew: המקריב - קבלה הוא, דתניא: "המקריב" — "והקריבו" — זה קבלת הדם:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:6:1.english: Who sacrifices - [This refers to] collection [of the blood], as it was taught in a baraita: "[Who] sacrifices [hamakriv]" — [and elsewhere,] "and they shall sacrifice [vehikrivu]" — this is the collection of the blood.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:8:1.hebrew: שכן פסולה בזר - לאפוקי שחיטה, שכשירה בזר, כדלקמן בפרק שלישי (זבחים דף לב.). ואף על פי ששחיטה וקבלה טעונות צפון, בפ' איזהו מקומן (לקמן זבחים דף מט.) יליף להו מקראי:
Rashi on Zevachim 4a:8:1.english: For it is invalid when performed by a non-priest - This excludes slaughter, which is valid when performed by a non-priest, as [stated] below in the third chapter (Zevachim 32a). And although slaughter and collection [of the blood] both require [being performed in] the north, in the chapter [entitled] Eizehu Mekoman (below, Zevachim 49a) he derives them from verses.

Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:13:1.hebrew: מה לזריקה שכן חייב עליה זר כו' - וא"ת: ונילף קבלה והולכה משחיטה וזריקה? וי"ל: מה להנך, שכן חייבין עליהן בחוץ, כדלקמן בשמעתין:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:13:1.english: "What about sprinkling, for a non-priest is liable for it," etc. - And if you say: Let us derive [the law of] receiving and conveying from slaughtering and sprinkling? One can answer: What [is unique] about those two, that [one is] liable [for performing] them outside [the Temple], as will be stated later in this passage:

Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:16:1.hebrew: דהולכה לא תפקה מכלל קבלה - וזריקה לא אתיא מכולהו, הדינים שישנן בחטאות הפנימיות:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:16:1.english: That conveying should not be excluded from the category of collection - But sprinkling cannot be derived from all of them, [namely, the laws] that apply to the inner sin offerings:

Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:19:1.hebrew: בא ללמד תודה ששחטה לשם שלמים כשרה - תימה: דבסוף כל הפסולין (לקמן זבחים דף לו.) דרשי' מיניה: "מנין לרבות שלמי נזיר ושלמי פסח? ת"ל 'שלמיו'", פי' דנאכלין ליום ולילה. וי"ל דהתם דריש מדכתביה גבי אכילה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:19:1.english: "It comes to teach that a thanks offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a peace offering is fit" - This is puzzling: for at the end of [the chapter] Kol HaPesulin (below, Zevachim 36a) we derive from it [the following]: "From where do we know to include the peace offerings of a nazirite and the peace offerings of Pesach? The verse states 'his peace offering'" — meaning, [offerings] that are eaten for a day and a night. And one can answer that there, [the Gemara] derives it from the fact that [the verse] wrote it in connection with eating.

Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:22:1.hebrew: ש"מ תרתי - וא"ת: ואימא כוליה זבח [להכי] הוא דאתא, שתהא זביחה לשם תודה? וי"ל: דאיכא לרבויי חטאת ואשם, מדכתיב ביה אכילה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:22:1.english: Learn two things from it - And if you ask: Say that the entire word "sacrifice" came for this purpose, [namely] that the slaughter must be for the sake of a thanks offering? And one can answer: That there is [a need] to include a sin offering and a guilt offering, since "eating" is written regarding it.

Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:27:1.hebrew: וישנן לאחר מיתה - אבל שינוי בעלים אינן לאחר מיתה. בפסחים (דף סא.) הקשה רבינו (דלמא מאחר): דשיעבודא לאו דאורייתא, כמו כן אין שינוי קודש לאחר מיתה — דמאי נפקא מינה דלא עלו לשם חובה? הא לא מיחייבי יורשין להביא אחר, דפלוגתא היא בקדושין בפ"ק (דף יג:) גבי האשה שהביאה חטאתה ומתה, יביאו יורשין עולתה; דקאמר שמואל: והוא שהפרישתה מחיים, ורב אשי אמר: אפי' שלא הפרישתה מחיים. והל"ל הכא, למ"ד שיעבודא [לאו] דאורייתא שאין שנוי קודש לאחר מיתה — תרתי מיהא דווקא? ויש לומר דנפקא מינה אם הפריש שתי שלמים או שתי עולות לאחריות ופירש, שאם אחת מתה או אבודה השניה תהיה קריבה עולה כדין הראשונה, ואם קרבה הראשונה כתקונה השניה תהיה חולין. וכי מתו בעלים ועשה יורש אחת שלא לשמה, הרי היא כאילו נאבדה וקרבה שניה תחתיה, ואם עשה הראשונה כתיקנה אז השניה חולין. אבל אם לא פירש כלום אלא סתם הפריש שתים לאחריות, אז אפילו נעשית הראשונה כתיקנה הוי שניה רועה, ודמיה קרבי עולה, כמו גבי מפריש שתי חטאות לאחריות כדאיתא לקמן (זבחים דף יא:): מותר חטאת קרב עולה, והכי נמי הוי בהפריש שתי שלמים או שתי עולות לאחריות. ועי"ל דלאחר מיתה הוי [איסור] בשינוי קודש כשמשנהו, אבל ליכא איסורא בשינוי בעלים כיון דליכא בעלים. מיהו אכתי לא ידע דרשא דמוצא שפתיך, דמינה נפקא איסור לשינוי קודש, מדמייתי לה בסמוך. הגה"ה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:27:1.english: And they apply after death - But a change of owner does not apply after death. In Pesachim (61a), our Rabbi raised a difficulty (perhaps [the reading is] "from another"): Since a lien is not a Torah-level [obligation], likewise there is no change of sanctity after death — for what difference does it make that they did not ascend for the sake of an obligation? The heirs are not obligated to bring another [offering]! For this is a dispute in Kiddushin, in the first chapter (13b), regarding the woman who brought her sin offering and died: the heirs bring her burnt offering. For Shmuel said: This is only if she set it aside during her lifetime; and Rav Ashi said: Even if she did not set it aside during her lifetime. So here, according to the one who says that a lien is [not] Torah-level, so that there is no change of sanctity after death, it should have said [that there are] at least two, specifically. And one can say that there is a practical difference if he set aside two peace offerings or two burnt offerings as a backup, and he specified: that if one dies or is lost, the second should be offered as a burnt offering like the first, and if the first is offered properly, the second should be unconsecrated. And if the owners died and the heir performed one not for its own sake, it is as though it were lost, and the second is offered in its place; and if he performed the first properly, then the second is unconsecrated. But if he specified nothing, and simply set aside two as a backup, then even if the first was performed properly, the second is left to graze, and its proceeds are offered as a burnt offering, like the case of one who sets aside two sin offerings as a backup, as stated below (Zevachim 11b): the remainder of a sin offering is offered as a burnt offering. And so too it is in the case of one who sets aside two peace offerings or two burnt offerings as a backup. Another answer: After death there is a [prohibition] in changing the sanctity when one changes it, but there is no prohibition in a change of owner, since there is no owner. However, he still did not know the teaching of "that which issues from your lips," from which the prohibition of a change of sanctity is derived, since he cites it shortly afterward. Gloss:

Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:27:2.hebrew: וישנן בציבור - משא"כ בשינוי בעלים, דאם שחט לשמו התמיד הרי הוא בעליו, ואפי' לשם עובד כוכבים לא מיפסיל, דבעינן חבירו דומיא דידיה מחוייב כפרה כמותו. ברו"ך:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:27:2.english: And it applies to a communal offering - This is not so with a change of owner: if one slaughtered the daily offering for its own sake, it is his [the public's] own, and even if [he slaughtered it] for the sake of a gentile, it is not disqualified, because we require [that the other person be] his fellow, similar to himself — one who is obligated to bring atonement just as he is. Blessed is He.

Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:5:1.hebrew: מה לזביחה שכן פוסל שלא לשם אוכלין בפסח - וא"ת: זריקה נמי תפסול מק"ו דשחיטה! שאינו פוסל בשינוי בעלים אלא על מנת לזרוק, ופוסלת על מנת שלא לשם אוכלין — ק"ו זריקה, שפוסלת בזורק שלא לשם בעלים, שתפסול שלא לשם אוכלין! וי"ל דאיכא למיפרך: מה לזביחה, שכן טעונה צפון, וישנה בחטאות הפנימיות. מיהו אכתי לא קמא ליה הך פירכא עד בסמוך, לכך י"ל דהכא לא יליף מזביחה אלא קבלה והולכה. ברו"ך. ועוד נראה דבפ' תמיד נשחט (פסחים דף סא.) ממעט שאר עבודות שלא [פסול] לשם אוכלין:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:5:1.english: "What about slaughter? It is unique in that it disqualifies [a Paschal offering] if not for the sake of those who eat it" - If you ask: Let sacrificial blood throwing also disqualify [when done not for the sake of those who eat], by an a fortiori argument from slaughter! For slaughter does not disqualify through a change of owner except when [the intent is] to throw [the blood] (i.e., with a further improper intent), yet it does disqualify with the intent [to slaughter] not for the sake of those who eat — so [with] blood throwing, which disqualifies when one throws not for the sake of the owners, all the more so it should disqualify when not for the sake of those who eat! One can answer that this can be refuted: What about slaughter? It is unique in that it requires the north, and it applies to the inner sin offerings. However, this refutation has not yet been stated until shortly afterward; therefore one can say that here [the Gemara] derives from slaughter only receiving and carrying. Barukh. Furthermore, it appears that in the chapter Tamid Nishchat (Pesachim 61a), [the Gemara] excludes the other rites from [being disqualified] if [done] not for the sake of those who eat.
